prerequisites: Mathematical prior knowledge in analysis and linear algebra is desirable.
Basic knowledge of physics and materials science.
A previous practice-oriented course 'strength of materials' and/or a course in applied mechanics.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with insight into the mechanical behavior of materials at a scientific level, specifically the theory of stress and strain tensors, elasticity theory, and plasticity theory.
Apply the scientific framework to provide insight into various aspects of crystal plasticity relevant to metals, namely dislocation behavior and plastic anisotropy.
Learn to understand a number of forming processes using the foregoing scientific framework.

syllabus_topics: Tensorial description of stresses and strains
Basis of elasticity theory (relation between stresses and strains, effect of crystal symmetry, field equations and solution methods, energy methods)
Classical mathematical plasticity theory up to Hill's theory for anisotropic materials
Introduction to the theory of dislocations in crystalline materials
Interactions between dislocations and between dislocations and other crystal defects
Explanation of material strengthening by plastic deformation
Application of plasticity laws to single crystals using the generalized Schmid law
Difference between ductile and brittle fracture
Classification of forming techniques using plastic deformation
Overview of methods for mathematical analysis of forming processes
In-depth treatment of some forming processes (rolling, sheet drawing, sheet deformation including local and diffuse necking)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of two theoretical questions and one calculation exercise. In the oral part, the worked-out solutions are reviewed and discussed. It is a closed-book exam, but a formula sheet is provided on site.
bibliography: Bundles with examples of solved exercises
